# Notebook setup

All analyses in this script use the full dataset (all 47 mats, 8 reef sites).
Colour- and substrate-based analyses are in 3.morphotypes.Rmd.

Outputs are numbered in the order they are produced:

- Figures: `figures/2.community/F<n>_<name>.pdf`
- Tables:  `outputs/2.community/T<n>_<name>.docx` (+ `.csv`)

```{r setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Only the packages used in this script are loaded.
# plyr is NOT loaded: attached after dplyr it masks summarise()/mutate() and ignores group_by().
# tidylog is loaded last so its dplyr wrappers are the active ones.
packages_used <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "scales",
                   "phyloseq", "microbiome", "vegan", "pairwiseAdonis", "MiscMetabar",
                   "dunn.test", "glmmTMB", "flextable", "officer", "beepr", "tidylog")

suppressMessages(invisible(
  lapply(packages_used, library, character.only = TRUE)
))

missing_pkgs <- setdiff(packages_used, .packages())
if (length(missing_pkgs) == 0) {
  message("All packages loaded correctly")
} else {
  message("Packages that did not load: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "))
}
rm(packages_used, missing_pkgs)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

# Same flextable defaults as in 3.morphotypes.Rmd
set_flextable_defaults(theme_fun = theme_vanilla, font.size = 10, bold_header = TRUE)

# Output folders
fig_dir <- "figures/2.community"
tab_dir <- "outputs/2.community"
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(tab_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Save a figure as PDF in fig_dir
save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 11, height = 11) {
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")), plot = plot,
         device = cairo_pdf, width = width, height = height, units = "in")
}

# Save one or more tables as one Word file (+ one csv per table) in tab_dir
save_tab <- function(tables, name) {
  if (is.data.frame(tables)) tables <- setNames(list(tables), name)
  doc <- read_docx()
  for (nm in names(tables)) {
    doc <- body_add_par(doc, nm, style = "Normal")
    doc <- body_add_flextable(doc, autofit(flextable(tables[[nm]])))
    doc <- body_add_par(doc, "")
  }
  print(doc, target = file.path(tab_dir, paste0(name, ".docx")))
  for (nm in names(tables)) {
    suffix <- if (length(tables) > 1) paste0("_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", nm)) else ""
    write.csv(tables[[nm]], file.path(tab_dir, paste0(name, suffix, ".csv")), row.names = FALSE)
  }
}

# Results table helper (rounded, optional "Source" column from row names)
to_table <- function(x, source_col = TRUE, digits = 4) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  if (source_col) x <- rownames_to_column(x, "Source")
  mutate(x, across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, digits)))
}

# Community matrix (samples as rows) from a phyloseq object, whatever its orientation
otu_matrix <- function(ps) {
  m <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) m <- t(m)
  m
}

# One definition of "unassigned" taxonomy, used by the heatmap and the core microbiome
is_unassigned <- function(x) {
  is.na(x) | x == "" |
    grepl("unknown|unidentified|uncultured|unclassified|metagenome", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
}

perm <- 9999   # permutations for PERMANOVA / PERMDISP

# p-value correction for ALL multiple comparisons in this script
# (Dunn tests, pairwise PERMANOVA, Hill number regressions). Same setting in 3.morphotypes.Rmd.
# "BH" = false discovery rate; "holm" = family-wise error rate.
p_adj_method <- "BH"

# Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn post-hoc test (two-sided, corrected with p_adj_method)
kw_dunn <- function(df, value, group, label = value) {
  kw <- kruskal.test(df[[value]] ~ factor(df[[group]]))
  invisible(capture.output(
    d <- dunn.test(df[[value]], factor(df[[group]]), method = tolower(p_adj_method),
                   altp = TRUE, kw = FALSE, table = FALSE)
  ))
  list(
    kw   = tibble(Index = label, Grouping = group, Chi2 = unname(kw$statistic),
                  df = unname(kw$parameter), p = kw$p.value),
    dunn = tibble(Index = label, Comparison = d$comparisons, Z = d$Z,
                  p = d$altP, p_adj = d$altP.adjusted)
  )
}

message(paste0(utf8::as_utf8("\U0001f600"), " All good!"))
beep(2)
```

# Introduction

The stacked (long) TSS dataframe is used for proportions, barplots and the heatmap. The TSS phyloseq object is used for the core microbiome, alpha and beta diversity.

# Data upload

Starting from the TSS stacked dataframe and the TSS phyloseq object.

```{r data upload, echo=FALSE}
taxa_stacked <- read.csv("data/ASV_taxa_stacked_tss.csv") %>%
  dplyr::rename(ASV = OTU) %>%
  select(-any_of(c("X", "X.1", "X.2")))

# Every site code must have a display name
stopifnot(all(unique(taxa_stacked$site) %in% names(site_labels)))

# Unassigned taxonomy -> "Unidentified"; site codes -> display names
taxa_stacked <- taxa_stacked %>%
  mutate(Phylum = ifelse(is_unassigned(Phylum), "Unidentified", Phylum),
         Genus  = ifelse(is_unassigned(Genus),  "Unidentified", Genus),
         site   = unname(site_labels[site]))

reef_tss <- readRDS("data/bcms_filtered&tss_reefs_raja2023.rds")

# Number of samples per site (used to average per site)
sample_n_site <- taxa_stacked %>%
  distinct(site, sample_id) %>%
  dplyr::count(site, name = "n_samples")

# ---- Checks ----
# 1. Each sample should sum to 1 (TSS)
summary(taxa_stacked %>%
          group_by(sample_id) %>%
          summarise(total = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
          pull(total))

# 2. Every sample should have the same number of rows (zeros kept)
if (n_distinct(dplyr::count(taxa_stacked, sample_id)$n) > 1)
  message("Samples have different numbers of rows: zeros may have been dropped from the stacked file")

# 3. Stacked file and phyloseq object should contain the same samples
setdiff(unique(taxa_stacked$sample_id), sample_names(reef_tss))
setdiff(sample_names(reef_tss), unique(taxa_stacked$sample_id))
```

## Community and environmental matrices

One community matrix and one environmental table are used for every test below (alpha diversity, PERMANOVA, PCoA, dbRDA), so all analyses use the same samples in the same order.

```{r matrices}
# Community matrix: samples as rows, ASVs as columns (empty ASVs removed)
community.matx <- otu_matrix(reef_tss)
community.matx <- community.matx[, colSums(community.matx) > 0, drop = FALSE]
dim(community.matx)

# Metadata in the same row order, with scaled environmental variables
# (only the four variables retained after the collinearity check)
env <- as(sample_data(reef_tss), "data.frame")
env <- env[rownames(community.matx), , drop = FALSE]
env <- env %>%
  mutate(sample_id   = rownames(community.matx),
         site        = factor(site_labels[site], levels = site_levels),
         DIN.scaled  = as.numeric(scale(DIN)),
         PO4.scaled  = as.numeric(scale(mean.PO4)),
         temp.scaled = as.numeric(scale(temperature)),
         chla.scaled = as.numeric(scale(chla)))
rownames(env) <- env$sample_id

stopifnot(identical(rownames(env), rownames(community.matx)),
          !anyNA(env$site))

# Environmental variables are measured per site: each site should have one value per variable
env %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(names(env_vars)), n_distinct), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r}
phylum_totals
```

```{r}
genus_totals
```

## Top 10 Phyla barplot

Prepare dataframe
```{r}
# Top 10 most abundant phyla overall (phylum_totals is already sorted)
top10_phyla <- head(phylum_totals$Phylum, 10)

# Collapse other phyla into "Other Phyla"
taxa_stacked_mod <- taxa_stacked %>%
  mutate(Phylum = ifelse(Phylum %in% top10_phyla, Phylum, "Other Phyla"))

# Percentage per site (pooled within site = mean across samples, since each sample sums to 1)
phylum_percentages <- taxa_stacked_mod %>%
  group_by(site, Phylum) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  mutate(percentage = 100 * total_abundance / sum(total_abundance)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Stacking order: preferred order first, any other top-10 phylum next,
# then Unidentified and Other Phyla (no phylum silently turns into NA)
phylum_order_pref <- c("Cyanobacteriota", "Proteobacteria", "Bacteroidota", "Planctomycetota",
                       "Crenarchaeota", "Verrucomicrobiota", "Actinobacteriota", "Acidobacteriota",
                       "Fusobacteriota", "Desulfobacterota", "Myxococcota", "Bdellovibrionota")
phylum_order <- c(intersect(phylum_order_pref, top10_phyla),
                  setdiff(top10_phyla, c(phylum_order_pref, "Unidentified")),
                  intersect("Unidentified", top10_phyla),
                  "Other Phyla")

missing_cols <- setdiff(phylum_order, names(all_colors))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0) message("Phyla without a colour: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))

phylum_percentages <- phylum_percentages %>%
  mutate(Phylum = factor(Phylum, levels = phylum_order),
         site   = factor(site, levels = site_levels))
```

Summary
```{r}
dominant_phyla <- c("Cyanobacteriota", "Proteobacteria", "Bacteroidota", "Planctomycetota")

# 1. Overall percentage per phylum (mean proportion of reads per sample)
overall <- phylum_percentages %>%
  group_by(Phylum) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(total_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(percentage = round(total / sum(total) * 100, 2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(percentage))
overall

# Combined % of the four dominant phyla
overall %>% filter(Phylum %in% dominant_phyla) %>% summarise(combined = sum(percentage))

# 2. Range across sites (min and max, with site names)
site_ranges <- phylum_percentages %>%
  filter(Phylum %in% dominant_phyla) %>%
  group_by(Phylum) %>%
  summarise(
    min_pct  = round(min(percentage), 2),
    min_site = site[which.min(percentage)],
    max_pct  = round(max(percentage), 2),
    max_site = site[which.max(percentage)],
    .groups  = "drop"
  )
site_ranges

# 3. Mean ± SD across samples (same basis as the overall %)
phylum_sample_stats <- taxa_stacked %>%
  group_by(sample_id, Phylum) %>%
  summarise(ra = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(sample_id, Phylum, fill = list(ra = 0)) %>%
  filter(Phylum %in% dominant_phyla) %>%
  group_by(Phylum) %>%
  summarise(mean_pct = round(mean(ra) * 100, 1),
            sd_pct   = round(sd(ra) * 100, 1),
            .groups  = "drop")
phylum_sample_stats

# 4. Wide table of site percentages (supplementary table)
site_table <- phylum_percentages %>%
  select(site, Phylum, percentage) %>%
  mutate(percentage = round(percentage, 2)) %>%
  arrange(site) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = site, values_from = percentage, values_fill = 0)
site_table

save_tab(site_table, "T1_phylum_percentages_site")
```

Plot
```{r}
phyla_stack_plot <-
  ggplot(phylum_percentages, aes(x = site, y = percentage, fill = Phylum)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = all_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Site", y = "Relative Abundance (%)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
phyla_stack_plot

save_fig(phyla_stack_plot, "F1_phyla_top10_site")
```

## Top 50 Genus

For results and supplements descriptions
```{r}
topN_genus <- 50

# Top 50 most abundant genera overall (genus_totals is already sorted)
top_genus <- unique(head(genus_totals$Genus, topN_genus))

# Collapse other genera into "Other genus" (with one shared phylum label, so it is not split across phyla)
Genus_percentages <- taxa_stacked %>%
  mutate(Genus  = ifelse(Genus %in% top_genus, Genus, "Other genus"),
         Phylum = ifelse(Genus == "Other genus", "Mixed", Phylum)) %>%
  group_by(site, Phylum, Genus) %>%
  summarise(total_abundance = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  mutate(percentage = 100 * total_abundance / sum(total_abundance)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Consistency check: no genus can exceed its own phylum at a site. Should return 0 rows.
phylum_site_full <- taxa_stacked %>%
  group_by(site, Phylum) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  mutate(phylum_pct = 100 * total / sum(total)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-total)

Genus_percentages %>%
  filter(Genus != "Other genus") %>%
  left_join(phylum_site_full, by = c("site", "Phylum")) %>%
  filter(percentage > phylum_pct + 1e-6)
```

#------------------------------

# Heatmap Community

Adjust the taxonomic value and the topN. TopN = Top most abundant of a defined range and taxonomic level.

```{r heatmap settings}
fill_level <- "Phylum"   # level used for the colour sidebar
taxa_level <- "Genus"    # level shown as heatmap rows
topN       <- 50
all        <- FALSE      # TRUE = plot every taxon instead of the top N
```

## Temporary df

```{r temporary dataframe}
# Site means = sum of relative abundance / number of samples in the site
toplot <- taxa_stacked %>%
  dplyr::rename(fill = all_of(fill_level), taxa = all_of(taxa_level)) %>%
  mutate(
    unident = is_unassigned(taxa),
    taxa    = ifelse(unident, "Unidentified", taxa),
    fill    = ifelse(unident, "Unidentified", fill)
  ) %>%
  group_by(site, taxa, fill) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(relative_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(sample_n_site, by = "site") %>%
  mutate(relative_abundance = total / n_samples) %>%
  select(-total, -n_samples) %>%
  # add explicit zeros so absent taxa get an "Absent" tile
  complete(nesting(taxa, fill), site, fill = list(relative_abundance = 0))

# Select the top N taxa by mean abundance across sites
if (all) topN <- n_distinct(toplot$taxa)

selected <- toplot %>%
  group_by(taxa) %>%
  summarise(meanAbun = mean(relative_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(meanAbun, n = topN, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  pull(taxa)

toplot <- toplot %>% filter(taxa %in% selected)
```

## Heatmap plot

Heatmap of the top 50 most abundant genera

```{r heatmap plot}
# Abundance classes: lower limits as proportions, labels in %
abund_breaks <- c(0, 0.0025, 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.10, Inf)
abund_labels <- c("<0.25", "0.25–0.5", "0.5–1", "1–2.5", "2.5–10", ">10")

abund_colors <- c(
  "Absent"          = "#FFFFFF",
  "<0.25"           = "#F2F2F2",
  "0.25–0.5"   = "#D1D1D1",
  "0.5–1"      = "#ADADAD",
  "1–2.5"      = "#878787",
  "2.5–10"     = "#585858",
  ">10"             = "#262626"
)

dark_classes <- c("2.5–10", ">10")  # these get white labels

heatmap_data <- toplot   # already one value per site and taxon

# Phylum order: by total abundance, Unidentified always last
heatmap_phylum_order <- heatmap_data %>%
  group_by(fill) %>%
  summarise(totalAbun = sum(relative_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(-totalAbun) %>%
  pull(fill)

heatmap_phylum_order <- c(
  heatmap_phylum_order[!grepl("Unidentified", heatmap_phylum_order)],
  heatmap_phylum_order[grepl("Unidentified", heatmap_phylum_order)]
)

# Genus order: grouped by phylum, highest to lowest within phylum.
# Reversed because ggplot draws y levels bottom-to-top.
taxa_order <- heatmap_data %>%
  mutate(fill = factor(fill, levels = heatmap_phylum_order)) %>%
  group_by(fill, taxa) %>%
  summarise(meanAbun = mean(relative_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(fill, -meanAbun) %>%
  pull(taxa) %>%
  unique() %>%
  rev()

# True zeros get their own "Absent" class; labels use 1 decimal, "<0.1" for tiny values, "–" for absent
heatmap_data <- heatmap_data %>%
  mutate(
    fill  = factor(fill, levels = heatmap_phylum_order),
    taxa  = factor(taxa, levels = taxa_order),
    site  = factor(site, levels = site_levels),
    abund_class = as.character(cut(relative_abundance, breaks = abund_breaks,
                                   labels = abund_labels, right = FALSE)),
    abund_class = ifelse(relative_abundance == 0, "Absent", abund_class),
    abund_class = factor(abund_class, levels = names(abund_colors)),
    cell_label  = case_when(
      relative_abundance == 0    ~ "–",
      relative_abundance < 0.001 ~ "<0.1",
      TRUE ~ as.character(round(relative_abundance * 100, 1))
    )
  )

# Checks
missing_phyla <- setdiff(levels(heatmap_data$fill), names(phylum_colors))
if (length(missing_phyla) > 0)
  message("Phyla missing from palette: ", paste(missing_phyla, collapse = ", "))

if (any(is.na(heatmap_data$site)))
  message("Sites not in site_levels: ",
          paste(setdiff(unique(toplot$site), site_levels), collapse = ", "))

# 1. Phylum sidebar
phylum_anno <- heatmap_data %>%
  distinct(taxa, fill) %>%
  mutate(x = 1)

p_phylum <- ggplot(phylum_anno, aes(x = x, y = taxa, fill = fill)) +
  geom_tile(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_colors, name = "Phylum") +
  labs(y = "Phylum") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 90, size = 12, face = "bold", vjust = 0.5))

# 2. Abundance heatmap
p_abund <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = site, y = taxa, fill = abund_class)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = cell_label, colour = abund_class %in% dark_classes),
            size = 4.25) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = abund_colors,
    drop   = FALSE,
    name   = "Relative\nAbundance (%)",
    guide  = guide_legend(
      reverse      = TRUE,
      override.aes = list(colour = "grey", linewidth = 0.3)
    )
  ) +
  labs(x = "Sampling Sites", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x      = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text.x       = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5,
                                     colour = "black", face = "bold", size = 11),
    axis.text.y       = element_text(colour = "black", face = "bold.italic", size = 11,
                                     hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
    axis.line         = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.75),
    axis.ticks        = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
    panel.grid        = element_blank(),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )

# 3. Combine
asv_heatmap <- p_phylum + p_abund +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.25, 12), guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.key = element_blank())

print(asv_heatmap)

save_fig(asv_heatmap, "F3_heatmap_top50_genus")
```

#------------------------------

# Core Microbiome

## Core ASVs

```{r core-members}
# Core: ASVs with abundance > 0 in more than 90% of samples
# (include.lowest = FALSE makes both cut-offs strict)
core_reef <- core_members(reef_tss, detection = 0,
                          prevalence = 0.90, include.lowest = FALSE)

length(core_reef)   # number of core ASVs
nsamples(reef_tss)     # number of samples
```

## Abundance and prevalence of the core ASVs

```{r core-data}
tax_df <- as.data.frame(as(tax_table(reef_tss), "matrix")) %>%
  rownames_to_column("ASV") %>%
  select(ASV, Phylum, Genus) %>%
  mutate(
    Phylum      = ifelse(is_unassigned(Phylum), "Unidentified", Phylum),
    genus_known = !is_unassigned(Genus)
  )

# Abundance matrix: samples as rows, core ASVs as columns
abund <- otu_matrix(reef_tss)[, core_reef, drop = FALSE]

# Overall summary per core ASV
core_summary <- tibble(
  ASV        = colnames(abund),
  Prevalence = colMeans(abund > 0),
  MeanAbund  = colMeans(abund)
) %>%
  left_join(tax_df, by = "ASV")

# Phyla ordered by number of core ASVs, Unidentified last
core_phylum_order <- core_summary %>% dplyr::count(Phylum, sort = TRUE) %>% pull(Phylum)
core_phylum_order <- c(setdiff(core_phylum_order, "Unidentified"), intersect(core_phylum_order, "Unidentified"))

# Labels: genus name if assigned (numbered if a genus has several core ASVs), otherwise the ASV ID
core_summary <- core_summary %>%
  mutate(Phylum = factor(Phylum, levels = core_phylum_order)) %>%
  arrange(Phylum, desc(MeanAbund)) %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  mutate(label = case_when(
    !genus_known ~ ASV,
    n() > 1      ~ paste(Genus, row_number()),
    TRUE         ~ Genus
  )) %>%
  ungroup()

core_summary
```

Save core summary as table

```{r core-table}
# Read share from unrounded values
core_share <- round(sum(core_summary$MeanAbund) * 100, 1)

core_table <- core_summary %>%
  arrange(Phylum, desc(MeanAbund)) %>%
  transmute(
    Phylum = as.character(Phylum),
    Genus  = ifelse(genus_known, Genus, "Unidentified"),
    ASV,
    `Prevalence (%)`              = round(Prevalence * 100, 1),
    `Mean relative abundance (%)` = round(MeanAbund * 100, 2)
  )

core_flex <- flextable(core_table) %>%
  italic(i = ~ Genus != "Unidentified", j = "Genus") %>%   # genus names in italics
  merge_v(j = "Phylum") %>%                               # one phylum label per block
  valign(j = "Phylum", valign = "top") %>%
  add_footer_lines(paste0(
    "Core ASVs present in more than 90% of samples (n = ", nsamples(reef_tss), "). ",
    "Together they account for ", core_share, "% of the reads.")) %>%
  autofit()
core_flex

save_as_docx("Core microbiome ASVs" = core_flex,
             path = file.path(tab_dir, "T2_core_microbiome_asvs.docx"))
write.csv(core_table, file.path(tab_dir, "T2_core_microbiome_asvs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Prevalence across detection thresholds

```{r core-thresholds, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9}
# Abundance matrix: ASVs as rows, samples as columns
abund_mat <- t(otu_matrix(reef_tss))

# ">0" and "0.01%" gave identical results, so 0.01% is left out
detections <- c(0, 0.0005, 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02)   # proportions
det_labels <- c(">0", "0.05", "0.1", "0.5", "1", "2")   # in %

# Prevalence of each core ASV at each detection threshold
core_thresh <- expand_grid(ASV = core_reef, Detection = detections) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(Prevalence = mean(abund_mat[ASV, ] > Detection)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(select(core_summary, ASV, label, genus_known, Phylum), by = "ASV")

# Robustness score: mean prevalence across all thresholds
robustness <- core_thresh %>%
  group_by(label) %>%
  summarise(score = mean(Prevalence), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(score)   # lowest first, so the most robust ends up on top

core_thresh <- core_thresh %>%
  mutate(
    label     = factor(label, levels = robustness$label),
    Detection = factor(Detection, levels = detections, labels = det_labels)
  )

# Genus names in italics, ASV IDs in plain text
italic_genera <- core_summary %>% filter(genus_known) %>% pull(label)
label_fun <- function(x) {
  parse(text = ifelse(x %in% italic_genera,
                      paste0("italic('", x, "')"),
                      paste0("'", x, "'")))
}

core_thresh.plot <- ggplot(core_thresh, aes(x = Detection, y = label, fill = Prevalence)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Prevalence * 100), colour = Prevalence > 0.6), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7F7F7", high = "#252525",
                      limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent,
                      name = "Prevalence") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = label_fun) +
  facet_grid(Phylum ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Detection threshold (% relative abundance)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(colour = "black", face = "bold", size = 10),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 9, colour = "black"),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )

core_thresh.plot

save_fig(core_thresh.plot, "F4_core_microbiome_thresholds", width = 8, height = 9)
```

#------------------------------

# Alpha diversity

## Hill numbers

Hill numbers are the number of equiprobable species giving the same diversity value as the observed distribution.

-   Hill number 0: Species richness
-   Hill number 1: Exponential of Shannon Index
-   Hill number 2: Inverse of Simpson Index

Using Package "MiscMetabar" (`hill_pq`). Note: the data are TSS-normalised, not rarefied, so richness (q = 0) is still sensitive to sequencing depth; q = 1 and q = 2 are much less affected.

```{r hill numbers}
# hill_pq returns one plot per Hill number; each plot's data holds all three Hill numbers per sample
hill_site <- hill_pq(reef_tss, "site", add_points = TRUE, one_plot = FALSE)
hill_raw  <- as.data.frame(hill_site[[1]][["data"]])
stopifnot(all(c("sample_id", names(hill_labels)) %in% names(hill_raw)))

# Hill numbers + display site names + environmental variables (from env, same samples as beta diversity)
hill_df <- hill_raw %>%
  select(sample_id, all_of(names(hill_labels))) %>%
  inner_join(env %>% select(sample_id, site, all_of(names(env_vars))), by = "sample_id")

stopifnot(nrow(hill_df) == nrow(env))

# Mean ± SD per site
hill_site_summary <- hill_df %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            across(Hill_0:Hill_2, list(mean = mean, sd = sd)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))
hill_site_summary
```

## Hill numbers across sites

Kruskal-Wallis test per Hill number, followed by two-sided Dunn tests corrected with `p_adj_method`

```{r hill site tests}
site_kwd <- lapply(names(hill_labels), function(h) kw_dunn(hill_df, h, "site", hill_labels[[h]]))

site_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(site_kwd, `[[`, "kw")) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
site_tests

site_pairwise <- bind_rows(lapply(site_kwd, `[[`, "dunn")) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
site_pairwise %>% filter(p_adj < 0.05)

save_tab(setNames(list(site_tests, site_pairwise),
                  c("Kruskal-Wallis across sites", paste0("Dunn tests (", p_adj_method, ")"))),
         "T3_hill_numbers_sites")
```

Plot

```{r hill site plot}
hill_long <- hill_df %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(hill_labels)), names_to = "hill", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(hill = factor(hill, levels = names(hill_labels)))

# Kruskal-Wallis result in each panel
hill_caption <- site_tests %>%
  mutate(hill  = factor(names(hill_labels), levels = names(hill_labels)),
         label = paste0("Kruskal-Wallis χ² = ", round(Chi2, 2),
                        ", df = ", df, ", p = ", signif(p, 2)))

hill_site_plot <- ggplot(hill_long, aes(x = site, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = site), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.7, size = 1.8) +
  geom_text(data = hill_caption, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
            hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_sites, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ hill, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", labeller = labeller(hill = hill_labels)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Effective number of ASVs") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
hill_site_plot

save_fig(hill_site_plot, "F5_hill_numbers_sites", width = 8, height = 10)
```

## Linear relationships vs env

Linear models of each Hill number against each retained environmental variable (DIN, PO₄³⁻, temperature, chl-a)

- The environmental variables are measured once per site, so the models are fitted on **site means** (n = 8 sites per model). Each site counts once, and the mats within a site are not treated as independent replicates.
- R² and p from `lm()`. Significance (*) uses p adjusted across the 12 models with `p_adj_method`.
- Model checks: residual normality (Shapiro-Wilk) per model and diagnostic plots below. With 8 points these checks have little power, so look at the plots for single sites with large leverage.

```{r hill site means}
# Mean (± SE) of each Hill number per site, plus the site's environmental values
hill_site_means <- hill_df %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(n_mats = n(),
            across(all_of(names(hill_labels)),
                   list(mean = mean, se = ~ sd(.x) / sqrt(n())), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"),
            across(all_of(names(env_vars)), first),
            .groups = "drop")
hill_site_means

# Long format: one row per site and Hill number
hill_site_long <- hill_site_means %>%
  select(site, n_mats, all_of(names(env_vars)), ends_with("_mean"), ends_with("_se")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = matches("^Hill_[0-9]_(mean|se)$"),
                      names_to = c("hill", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "^(Hill_[0-9])_(mean|se)$")
```

```{r hill env models}
lm_results <- expand_grid(hill = names(hill_labels), env_var = names(env_vars)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    fit       = list(lm(reformulate(env_var, response = "mean"),
                        data = hill_site_long[hill_site_long$hill == hill, ])),
    n_sites   = nobs(fit),
    slope     = coef(fit)[[2]],
    R2        = summary(fit)$r.squared,
    p         = summary(fit)$coefficients[2, 4],
    Shapiro_p = shapiro.test(residuals(fit))$p.value
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = p_adj_method),
         sig   = p_adj < 0.05)

lm_table <- lm_results %>%
  transmute(Index = hill_labels[hill], Variable = env_vars[env_var],
            n_sites, slope, R2, p, p_adj, Shapiro_p) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
lm_table

save_tab(lm_table, "T4_hill_numbers_env_models")
```

Model diagnostics (residuals vs fitted and QQ plot for each model)

```{r hill env diagnostics, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 9}
op <- par(mfrow = c(3, 8), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(lm_results))) {
  plot(lm_results$fit[[i]], which = 1:2, caption = "",
       main = paste(lm_results$hill[i], "~", lm_results$env_var[i]), cex.main = 0.7)
}
par(op)
```

Panel figure: rows are Hill numbers, columns are environmental variables. Points are site means ± SE. Every model has its regression line; significant regressions (adjusted p < 0.05) are blue, non-significant ones grey.

```{r hill env plot}
plot_df <- hill_site_long %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(names(env_vars)), names_to = "env_var", values_to = "env_value") %>%
  left_join(select(lm_results, hill, env_var, sig), by = c("hill", "env_var")) %>%
  mutate(hill    = factor(hill, levels = names(hill_labels)),
         env_var = factor(env_var, levels = names(env_vars)))

lab_df <- lm_results %>%
  transmute(hill    = factor(hill, levels = names(hill_labels)),
            env_var = factor(env_var, levels = names(env_vars)),
            sig,
            label   = paste0("R² = ", sprintf("%.2f", R2), ifelse(sig, "*", "")))

hill_env_plot <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = env_value, y = mean, colour = sig, fill = sig)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
              linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), width = 0, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_text(data = lab_df, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label, colour = sig),
            hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#2166AC", `FALSE` = "grey45"), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#2166AC", `FALSE` = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  facet_grid(hill ~ env_var, scales = "free", switch = "both",
             labeller = labeller(hill = hill_labels, env_var = env_vars)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.placement  = "outside",
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
hill_env_plot

save_fig(hill_env_plot, "F6_hill_numbers_env_regressions", width = 12, height = 9)
```

#-------------------------------

# Beta diversity

## Bray-Curtis distance matrix

```{r bray}
bray_dist <- vegdist(community.matx, method = "bray")
```

## PERMANOVA across sites

```{r permanova sites}
permanova.site <- adonis2(community.matx ~ site,
                          data = env,
                          permutations = perm,
                          method = "bray")
permanova.site

# Homogeneity of multivariate dispersion (PERMDISP).
# PERMANOVA can be significant because of differences in spread, not only in location;
# a non-significant PERMDISP supports interpreting the site effect as a compositional difference.
disp_site <- betadisper(bray_dist, env$site)
permdisp_site <- permutest(disp_site, permutations = perm)
permdisp_site

# Pairwise PERMANOVA between sites (corrected with p_adj_method)
pairwise_site <- pairwise.adonis(community.matx,
                                 factors    = as.character(env$site),
                                 sim.method = "bray",
                                 p.adjust.m = p_adj_method,
                                 perm       = perm) %>%
  to_table(source_col = FALSE) %>%
  arrange(p.adjusted, desc(R2))
pairwise_site

save_tab(list("PERMANOVA site"            = to_table(permanova.site),
              "PERMDISP site"             = to_table(permdisp_site$tab),
              "Pairwise PERMANOVA"        = pairwise_site),
         "T5_permanova_sites")
```

Pairwise effect sizes

```{r pairwise plot}
pairwise_effectsize_site <- pairwise_site %>%
  mutate(pairs = reorder(pairs, R2)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = R2, y = pairs, colour = p.adjusted < 0.05)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey50", `TRUE` = "#b02b25")) +
  labs(x = "Effect size (R²)", y = NULL, colour = paste0("Significant (", p_adj_method, " p < 0.05)")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
pairwise_effectsize_site

save_fig(pairwise_effectsize_site, "F7_pairwise_permanova_sites", width = 8, height = 10)
```

## PCoA (unconstrained)

```{r pcoa}
pcoa_result <- cmdscale(bray_dist, eig = TRUE, k = 2)

# % variance explained (negative eigenvalues from Bray-Curtis are set to 0 in the total)
eig_pos  <- pmax(pcoa_result$eig, 0)
var_expl <- round(100 * eig_pos / sum(eig_pos), 1)

pcoa_df <- data.frame(
  Axis1 = pcoa_result$points[, 1],
  Axis2 = -pcoa_result$points[, 2],   # axis flipped for display
  env
)
```

Plot

```{r pcoa plot}
pcoa_plot <-
  ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = Axis1, y = Axis2, shape = site)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, stroke = 1.1, colour = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shape_sites, name = "Site") +
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = "black", size = 4, alpha = 0.6))) +
  labs(x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_expl[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_expl[2], "%)"),
       title = "PCoA (Bray-Curtis)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid = element_blank())
pcoa_plot

save_fig(pcoa_plot, "F8_pcoa_sites", width = 8, height = 8)
```

#-------------------------------

# dbRDA

Distance-based RDA (Bray-Curtis) with the four environmental variables retained after the collinearity check: DIN, PO₄³⁻, temperature and chl-a.

The variables are measured per site, so the constrained part of the model can only explain differences between sites (at most 7 df). The model is therefore a test of how much of the between-site variation these four variables account for.

```{r dbrda}
dbrda_env <- capscale(community.matx ~ DIN.scaled + PO4.scaled + temp.scaled + chla.scaled,
                      data = env, distance = "bray")
dbrda_env
RsquareAdj(dbrda_env)

# Collinearity inside the model (VIF > 10 is usually a problem)
vif.cca(dbrda_env)
```

## ANOVA

`by = "terms"` is sequential (depends on the order of the predictors); `by = "margin"` tests each predictor after all others and does not depend on the order, so it is used for the arrow significance in the plot.

```{r dbrda anova}
anova(dbrda_env, permutations = 999)                # overall model
anova(dbrda_env, permutations = 999, by = "axis")   # per axis
anova(dbrda_env, permutations = 999, by = "terms")  # sequential
anova(dbrda_env, permutations = 999, by = "margin") # marginal
```

## Partial dbRDA

Each variable tested after removing the effect of the other three.

```{r partial dbrda}
env_terms <- c("DIN.scaled", "PO4.scaled", "temp.scaled", "chla.scaled")

partial_dbrda <- lapply(env_terms, function(v) {
  f <- as.formula(paste("community.matx ~", v, "+ Condition(",
                        paste(setdiff(env_terms, v), collapse = " + "), ")"))
  m <- capscale(f, data = env, distance = "bray")
  a <- anova(m, permutations = 999)
  tibble(Variable = v,
         Adj_R2   = RsquareAdj(m)$adj.r.squared,
         F        = a$F[1],
         p        = a$`Pr(>F)`[1])
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
partial_dbrda
```

## Save tables

```{r dbrda tables}
rsq <- RsquareAdj(dbrda_env)
s   <- summary(dbrda_env)

dbrda_r2 <- data.frame(Metric = c("R2", "Adj_R2"),
                       Value  = c(rsq$r.squared, rsq$adj.r.squared)) %>%
  mutate(Value = round(Value, 4))

dbrda_inertia <- data.frame(
  Metric     = c("Total", "Constrained", "Unconstrained"),
  Inertia    = c(s$tot.chi, s$constr.chi, s$unconst.chi),
  Proportion = c(s$tot.chi, s$constr.chi, s$unconst.chi) / s$tot.chi
) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))

dbrda_overall <- to_table(anova(dbrda_env, permutations = 999))
dbrda_axis    <- to_table(anova(dbrda_env, permutations = 999, by = "axis"))
dbrda_margin  <- to_table(anova(dbrda_env, permutations = 999, by = "margin"))
dbrda_vif     <- data.frame(Variable = names(vif.cca(dbrda_env)),
                            VIF      = round(vif.cca(dbrda_env), 2))

save_tab(list("R2"                          = dbrda_r2,
              "Partitioning of inertia"     = dbrda_inertia,
              "Overall model"               = dbrda_overall,
              "Axes"                        = dbrda_axis,
              "Marginal tests"              = dbrda_margin,
              "Partial dbRDA"               = partial_dbrda,
              "VIF"                         = dbrda_vif),
         "T6_dbrda_env")
```

## Df for plot

```{r dbrda df}
dbrda_scoresdf <- scores(dbrda_env, display = "sites") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
  left_join(env %>% select(sample_id, site), by = "sample_id")

# Arrows, coloured by marginal significance
var_labels <- c(DIN.scaled  = "DIN",
                PO4.scaled  = "PO[4]^'3-'",
                temp.scaled = "Temperature",
                chla.scaled = "'Chl-a'")

vectorsig <- scores(dbrda_env, display = "bp") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("variable") %>%
  left_join(dbrda_margin %>% transmute(variable = Source, significant = `Pr(>F)` < 0.05),
            by = "variable") %>%
  mutate(label = var_labels[variable])

# % of total variation per constrained axis
cap_expl <- round(100 * dbrda_env$CCA$eig / dbrda_env$tot.chi, 1)
```

## Plot

```{r dbrda plot}
dbrda_plot <-
  ggplot(dbrda_scoresdf, aes(x = CAP1, y = CAP2, shape = site)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, stroke = 1.1, colour = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shape_sites, name = "Site") +
  geom_segment(data = vectorsig,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = CAP1, yend = CAP2, colour = significant),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm")),
               linewidth = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = vectorsig,
            aes(x = CAP1 * 1.12, y = CAP2 * 1.12, label = label, colour = significant,
                fontface = ifelse(significant, "bold", "plain")),parse = TRUE,
            size = 4, inherit.aes = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#2166AC", `FALSE` = "black"),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = "p < 0.05", `FALSE` = "p > 0.05"),
                      name = "Marginal test") +
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = "black", size = 4, alpha = 0.6))) +
  labs(x = paste0("dbRDA1 (", cap_expl[1], "% of total)"),
       y = paste0("dbRDA2 (", cap_expl[2], "% of total)"),
       title = "dbRDA (Bray-Curtis)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",panel.grid = element_blank())
dbrda_plot

save_fig(dbrda_plot, "F9_dbrda_env", width = 8, height = 8)
```

#-------------------------------

# PCoA + dbRDA

Panel with the unconstrained PCoA (left) and the dbRDA (right).

```{r pcoa dbrda panel}
pcoa_dbrda_panel <- (pcoa_plot + labs(title = "A. Unconstrained PCoA")) +
  (dbrda_plot + labs(title = "B. Constrained (dbRDA)")) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "right")
pcoa_dbrda_panel

save_fig(pcoa_dbrda_panel, "F10_pcoa_dbrda_panel", width = 11, height = 6)
```
